h: Remembrance and Inscription: The Insertions of the Yamim Nora'im Prayer

p: in the blessing of Avos we say
in the blessing of Atah Gibbor
and in Sim Shalom we say
the language of both remembrance and inscription:
the change of wording in the blessing of Modim,
where we say "all the children of Your covenant."
that, as is known, of the eighteen blessings
to the twelve tribes of Kah,
"And they shall sanctify the Holy One of Yaakov";
for the three attributes Chessed, Gevurah, Tiferes.
And they are like a servant
who sets out his master's praise before him;
who has received a reward from his master, etc.
and they correspond to Netzach, Hod, Yesod.
The blessing "Who returns His Shechinah to Tziyon"
Hod is the level of Aharon;
and they are the groomsman of the King
and the groomsman of the Queen,
as is written in the holy Zohar;
"For all that is in heaven and on earth"
"who holds on to heaven and to earth";
Kudsha Brich Hu and His Shechinah.
'and to the earth' — this is the body."
Now in the blessing of Atah Kadosh,
שֶׁהוּא הַבְּרִיחַ הַתִּיכוֹן וְגוֹ׳ (שְׁמוֹת כו, כח),
we make no request at all;
and likewise in the blessing of Avodah,
as it is stated in the Tikkunei Zohar
Rather, he was from the inner side:
and that one from the soul" —
there too we mention nothing at all,
is "a place that has no forgetting
and forgetting does not exist in it,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב צב, ב),
"'Zachor' is for the male, and this is the brain";
and it corresponds to the soul,
And inscription, which is already revealed,
and it corresponds to the attribute of Yesod.
and "inscribe us" corresponding to the body;
and we say "in the Book of Life,"
according to what we have said
the bodies and souls of Yisrael;
"And all your deeds are written in a book" —
in the bodies and souls of Yisrael.
Afterward, in the blessing of Atah Gibbor,
to be born in the holiness of Yisrael;
which resemble one who receives a reward from his master,
we say in the blessing of thanksgiving,
who is the groomsman of the Queen:
since "there is no good but Torah"
and we say "all the children of Your covenant,"
in the blessings of Avos and Gevuros,
where the language of remembrance is mentioned,
which is "a place that has no forgetting,"
there is no need to say
for then "there will be no survivor
and there will be only Yisrael.
And this is why we say
"Who remembers His creatures for life in mercy."
Likewise in "Remember us" it does not specify at all,
as it was at the giving of the Torah.
Afterward, in the blessing of Sim Shalom,
we say "may we be remembered and inscribed,"
corresponding to the soul and the body;
and all Your people, the house of Yisrael,"
within the totality of Bnei Yisrael;
and we also specify "the house of Yisrael."

Heaven and earth: soul and body
Why nothing is inserted for Yaakov and Moshe
Zachor: the soul in the brain
Sim Shalom: both, for body and soul

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 9 — “The first three blessings are the holiness of the Avos: ‘Shield of Avraham,’ then ‘You are mighty’ corresponding to the Fear of Yitzchak, then ‘You are holy’ corresponding to Yaakov, as it says, ‘They will sanctify the Holy One of Yaakov’… and afterward the twelve middle blessings corresponding to the holiness of the twelve tribes, as written in the Raya Mehemna (Zohar III 4a).” Connection: Both map the blessings of the Amidah onto the Avos and the tribes to explain where each insertion belongs.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 34a — "Rabbi Chanina said: The first [blessings] are like a servant who sets out praise before his master; the middle ones are like a servant who requests a reward from his master; the last are like a servant who has received a reward from his master, takes his leave and goes."

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 91b — "So too the Holy One brings the soul, casts it into the body, and judges them together, as it says, 'He calls to the heavens above, and to the earth, to judge His people' (Tehillim 50:4): 'He calls to the heavens above' — this is the soul; 'and to the earth, to judge His people' — this is the body."

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah 16b — "Rabbi Kruspedai said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: Three books are opened on Rosh Hashanah: one of the completely wicked, one of the completely righteous, and one of the intermediate. The completely righteous are written and sealed immediately for life; the completely wicked are written and sealed immediately for death; the intermediate are held in suspense from Rosh Hashanah until Yom Kippur: if they merit, they are written for life; if they do not merit, they are written for death."

paragraphs.text: Chagigah 3a — “Rava expounded: What is meant by ‘How beautiful are your steps in sandals, daughter of the generous one’? How beautiful are Israel’s feet when they go up for the festival pilgrimage. ‘Daughter of the generous one’—the daughter of Avraham our father, who is called generous, as it is said, ‘The generous ones of the peoples gathered, the people of the God of Avraham.’ ‘The God of Avraham,’ and not the God of Yitzchak and Yaakov? Rather, the God of Avraham, who was the first of the converts.” The Gemara explains why this verse names Avraham particularly. Rav Tzadok compares this particular naming with the Zohar’s inclusive application to the patriarchs.
